title: release: add signing stage for offline bundles (KMS/HSM-backed) + upload detached signatures
author: Sahana Iyer
body: ## Summary This adds a dedicated signing stage to the release pipeline for Redwood Private offline bundles. The stage signs bundle-level artifacts using the KMS/HSM-backed signing key and publishes detached signatures alongside the existing bundle outputs in artifact storage. Verification is fully offline; we do not rely on transparency logs or external calls. ## Why Regulated/air-gapped customers are moving bundles via removable media/offline repos and need integrity + provenance guarantees. This stage is the build-side prerequisite for installer verification (ENG-3914) and break-glass policy enforcement (ENG-3915). ## What changes - Adds a `sign_offline_bundle` step in the release pipeline that runs after bundle assembly and before publish. - Uses the KMS-backed signer via the CI signing service identity (no long-lived credentials; OIDC to assume the release signer role). - Produces detached signatures for: (1) `offline-bundle-<version>.tar.zst` (2) `bundle.manifest.json` (3) `checksums.txt` - Uploads `*.sig` and `signing-metadata.json` adjacent to artifacts (same prefix) so the installer can fetch/verify offline from the transferred directory. - Hard fail if signing cannot be performed (fail-closed); no auto-fallback to unsigned artifacts. ## Storage layout (unchanged, extended) `releases/<version>/offline-bundles/<bundle-id>/` now includes: - `offline-bundle-<version>.tar.zst` - `offline-bundle-<version>.tar.zst.sig` - `bundle.manifest.json` - `bundle.manifest.json.sig` - `checksums.txt` - `checksums.txt.sig` - `signing-metadata.json` (key id + algorithm + signing tool version + CI build id) ## Notes / security - Key is referenced by alias only (e.g., `kms://alias/redwood-offline-bundle-signer`); the exact key material stays in KMS/HSM. - Pipeline restricts signing step to release tags and the `release` Buildkite queue; the step requires the dedicated `redwood-release-signer` role. - Signature algorithm: ECDSA P-256 (as currently provisioned in KMS). - The step logs key id (opaque), artifact names, and resulting signature filenames; it does not log raw signatures or payload bytes. ## Testing - Ran release pipeline in staging with a test KMS key alias; confirmed `*.sig` uploads and that signature inputs are stable across retries when artifacts are unchanged. - Added a small unit test for the signing script to ensure we sign the intended set of files and fail if any target is missing. ## Rollout - Merge behind `RELEASE_SIGN_OFFLINE_BUNDLES=1` (default on for release tags once key policy is approved). - After merge: Security/Infra to finalize prod key policy (INT-662) and we will flip the default for prod releases. ## Checklist - [x] Signing step uses OIDC / no static secrets - [x] Fail-closed on signing/upload errors - [x] Detached signatures colocated with artifacts - [x] Minimal logging (no sensitive material) - [ ] Follow-up: add signer key rotation doc + tooling (ENG-3919)
commits: release/signing: include signing-metadata.json in published outputs
tests: unit test for signing target set + fail-closed behavior
docs(ci): note required IAM/KMS permissions for signer role
review_conversation: Connor O'Brien (Release Eng) [2024-03-05]: This is the right shape. Two asks: (1) ensure we sign the manifest + checksums as well as the tarball, otherwise installer will have to special-case. (2) make sure the signing step runs before publish so we never publish unsigned bundles if signing fails.

Sahana Iyer (author) [2024-03-05]: Updated: now signs `bundle.manifest.json` + `checksums.txt` in addition to the tarball. Also reordered pipeline so signing occurs before the publish/upload group; publish is gated on signature generation + upload.

Hanae Suzuki (KMS/Secrets) [2024-03-05]: Please don’t reference the full key ARN in logs/config. Use alias only. Also confirm CI uses OIDC role assumption and does not require storing AWS creds as secrets.

Sahana Iyer (author) [2024-03-05]: Done. Config now uses `kms://alias/redwood-offline-bundle-signer`. Logs print the alias + KMS key id hash from signer output, no ARN. CI uses OIDC to assume `redwood-release-signer` and fails if role assumption isn’t available.

Marcus Lin (Security) [2024-03-06]: +1. Please tighten failure modes: signing must be fail-closed and MUST NOT proceed to publish on partial success. Also request a small metadata file that records algorithm + key alias + signing tool version for audit evidence.

Sahana Iyer (author) [2024-03-06]: Added `signing-metadata.json` and made the step atomic: if any target fails signing OR any signature upload fails, the step exits non-zero and pipeline stops before publish. Partial signature sets are cleaned up from the workspace.

Priya Natarajan (Platform) [2024-03-06]: Nit: the signing script currently hardcodes the list of files. That’s OK for v1, but please add a comment that this list is intentionally explicit for auditability.
Sahana Iyer (author) [2024-03-06]: Added comment + link to ENG-3913/ADR draft in script header. Keeping explicit list to avoid accidentally signing unexpected outputs.
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng) [2024-03-07]: Approved. Please coordinate the prod key policy change under INT-662 before enabling by default for prod tags.
Marcus Lin (Security) [2024-03-07]: Approved after updates. Ensure the break-glass story remains installer-side only; release pipeline should not support skipping signing.
notable_incidents: Initial CI run failed in staging due to missing `kms:Sign` permission on the assumed role; fixed by updating the staging role policy and reran successfully.
release_notes: Release pipeline now signs Redwood Private offline bundle artifacts using a KMS/HSM-backed key and publishes detached signatures (+ signing metadata) alongside bundles for offline verification.
